title: React TypeScript Applied Check
description: Apply React TypeScript knowledge to nullable state, typed events, generic components, reducer actions, context safety, discriminated unions, and common mistakes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A component starts with `const [user, setUser] = useState(null);` and later calls `setUser({ id: '1', name: 'Ada' })`. What is the best fix?

options.text: Store the user in a CSS class

questions.explanation: When the initial value is null, TypeScript needs the intended future state type explicitly.

questions.prompt: Which prop type best models a button callback that receives an id?
questions.explanation: Callback props should describe their parameters and return type. Event-like props commonly return void.

questions.prompt: Given `type Props = { kind: 'link'; href: string } | { kind: 'button'; onClick: () => void }`, what enables narrowing?
questions.explanation: The shared `kind` field is the discriminant. Checking it lets TypeScript know which variant is active.

questions.prompt: Which reducer action design choices improve type safety? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use literal action types such as `{ type: 'add'; item: Item }`
Make each action carry only the payload it needs
Use a union of action object types
Use `{ type: string; payload: any }` for all actions

questions.explanation: Discriminated unions for reducer actions let TypeScript narrow payloads and catch invalid dispatches.

questions.prompt: A generic list component accepts `items` and `renderItem`. Which signature is most useful?

options.text: `function List<T>({ items, renderItem }: { items: T[]; renderItem: (item: T) => React.ReactNode })`

questions.explanation: A generic keeps the item type connected between the array and render callback.

questions.prompt: Typing an API result as `User` after `await response.json()` proves the server sent a valid `User` at runtime.
questions.explanation: A TypeScript annotation or assertion does not validate runtime data. Use schema validation or defensive checks when external data is untrusted.

questions.prompt: In a form submit handler, why call `event.preventDefault()` after typing `event: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>`?

options.text: To stop the browser's default full page form submission
To make TypeScript infer CSS classes
To convert the form into a reducer
To force all inputs to be uncontrolled

questions.explanation: Typing the event helps access form event APIs safely, and preventDefault keeps React in control of the submit flow.

questions.prompt: A context is created as `createContext<AuthContextValue | null>(null)`. Which consumer pattern is safest?

options.text: Use a `useAuth()` hook that checks for null and throws if the provider is missing
Cast the value to `any` in every component
Store auth state in the component name

questions.explanation: The custom hook keeps the nullable setup internal and gives all consumers a consistent, clear provider-missing error.
